products.name: Active DisplayPort to HDMI 4K60 adapter
products.headline: DP source → HDMI display
products.fit: active conversion · 4K 60Hz · choose standard or HDR10
products.summary: One active StarTech.com adapter for connecting a DisplayPort computer or dock to one HDMI monitor, television, or projector at up to 3840 by 2160 at 60 Hz. It is directional and does not connect an HDMI source to a DisplayPort display. Choose DP2HD4K60S for standard HDMI 2.0 output or DP2HD4K60H when the complete source-to-display chain supports HDR10 over HDMI 2.0b.

sharedSpecs.name: Not reversible
sharedSpecs.value: Does not convert an HDMI source to a DisplayPort display

sharedSpecs.name: Not for
sharedSpecs.value: 4K 120Hz, HDMI 2.1, multiple displays, USB-C sources, or HDMI-to-DisplayPort conversion

faqs.q: Does this adapter connect a DisplayPort computer to an HDMI monitor?
faqs.a: Yes. The DisplayPort male plug connects to the source computer, graphics card, or compatible dock, and an HDMI cable connects the adapter's HDMI female port to the display.

faqs.q: Can this adapter convert HDMI to DisplayPort?
faqs.a: No. Both variants work only from a DisplayPort source to an HDMI display.

faqs.q: Which variant should I choose for HDR10?
faqs.a: Choose DP2HD4K60H. HDR10 also requires a DisplayPort 1.4 source, compatible content, a suitable HDMI cable, and an HDMI 2.0b HDR display. DP2HD4K60S has no HDR10 claim.

faqs.q: What is required for 4K at 60 Hz?
faqs.a: Use a compatible DisplayPort source, a 4K60-capable HDMI display, and an HDMI cable rated for the required 18 Gbps link. Lower-capability equipment can reduce the resolution or refresh rate.

faqs.q: Does the source need dual-mode DisplayPort or DP++?
faqs.a: No. These are active adapters and support standard DisplayPort and DP++ sources within the maker's published requirements.

faqs.q: Does this adapter support 4K at 120 Hz?
faqs.a: No. The published maximum is 3840 by 2160 at 60 Hz.

specs.name: HDR
specs.value: HDR10; full source, content, cable and display support required

specs.name: Compatibility note
specs.value: Some NVIDIA combinations may restrict 4:4:4 chroma or 5.1/7.1 audio

products.name: Active HDMI to DisplayPort 4K30 adapter
products.headline: HDMI source → DisplayPort display
products.summary: One StarTech.com HD2DP active converter for connecting an HDMI source to one DisplayPort monitor or projector. The HDMI male plug carries video from the source, the DisplayPort female port accepts the display cable, and USB supplies power. It is not the common reverse-direction DisplayPort-to-HDMI adapter.

specs.name: Not reversible
specs.value: Does not connect a DisplayPort source to an HDMI display

specs.name: Not for
specs.value: 4K 60Hz, HDCP 2.2-protected 4K playback, DisplayPort-to-HDMI conversion, or multiple displays

faqs.q: Is this an HDMI to DisplayPort adapter or DisplayPort to HDMI adapter?
faqs.a: It is HDMI source to DisplayPort display. It is specifically for the less common reverse direction and is not interchangeable with a DisplayPort-to-HDMI adapter.

faqs.q: Why does the HD2DP adapter need USB?
faqs.a: USB powers the active signal converter. The USB connection does not carry the video signal.

faqs.q: Will HD2DP show 4K at 60 Hz?
faqs.a: No. Its published 4K maximum is 3840 by 2160 at 30 Hz.

faqs.q: Will this adapter play HDCP 2.2-protected 4K streaming video?
faqs.a: No. StarTech.com states that HD2DP does not support HDCP 2.2.

faqs.q: What connects to each end?
faqs.a: Connect the HDMI male plug to the source, a DisplayPort cable from the female DisplayPort output to the display, and USB to a powered USB port.

products.name: Active DVI-D to DisplayPort adapter
products.headline: DVI-D source → DisplayPort display
products.summary: One StarTech.com DVI2DP2 active converter for connecting a digital DVI-D source to one DisplayPort monitor or projector. The built-in USB lead supplies power only. Its conservative published ceiling is 1920 by 1200 at 60 Hz, and it does not convert analog DVI-A or VGA.

specs.name: Power
specs.value: Built-in 8 in USB power lead; 24 in USB extension included

specs.name: USB signal role
specs.value: Power only; no video or data

specs.name: Audio
specs.value: No audio claim; DVI input is treated as video

specs.name: Not reversible
specs.value: Does not connect a DisplayPort source to a DVI display

specs.name: Not for
specs.value: Analog DVI-A, VGA, DisplayPort-to-DVI conversion, 4K, or audio-dependent installations

faqs.q: Does DVI2DP2 connect an older DVI computer to a DisplayPort monitor?
faqs.a: Yes, when the source supplies a compatible digital DVI-D signal. The DisplayPort female side connects to the monitor cable.

faqs.q: Can this adapter connect a DisplayPort computer to a DVI monitor?
faqs.a: No. DVI2DP2 works only from a DVI-D source to a DisplayPort display.

faqs.q: Does the USB cable carry video?
faqs.a: No. The USB lead powers the active converter and carries no video or user data.

faqs.q: Will DVI2DP2 convert analog DVI or VGA?
faqs.a: No. It requires a digital DVI-D source signal.

faqs.q: What is the maximum supported resolution?
faqs.a: The conservative manufacturer-published maximum is 1920 by 1200 at 60 Hz.

products.name: USB-B panel-mount extension cable
products.headline: USB-B female panel → USB-B male
products.summary: One StarTech.com USBPNLBFBM3 shielded extension cable for placing a USB-B female port on a custom enclosure, kiosk, instrument panel, or internally mounted USB-B device. The user-facing end is USB-B female and the internal device end is USB-B male. It is USB 2.0, not USB 3.x.

specs.name: Measure before ordering
specs.value: Panel opening, screw spacing, rear connector depth, and cable bend clearance

specs.name: Not for
specs.value: USB-A panels, USB-C, USB 3.x speeds, or an ordinary USB-A-to-B printer connection

faqs.q: Which USB-B connector mounts on the outside of the panel?
faqs.a: The USB-B female connector is the panel-mounted user-facing port. The USB-B male connector attaches to the internal device.

faqs.q: Is USBPNLBFBM3 a USB 3.0 cable?
faqs.a: No. It is USB 2.0 with a stated maximum data rate of 480 Mbps.

faqs.q: How long is the USB-B panel-mount extension?
faqs.a: It is 3 feet, or 91.4 centimeters, from end to end.

faqs.q: What should I measure before cutting an enclosure?
faqs.a: Confirm the panel opening and screw spacing against the physical product, then leave space for the approximately 1.5 by 0.6 inch connector body and for the cable to bend without stressing the strain relief.

faqs.q: Can this replace a standard USB-A to USB-B printer cable?
faqs.a: No. Both ends use USB-B geometry: one female panel port and one male internal-device plug.

products.name: DisplayPort to Mini DisplayPort adapter cable
products.headline: DP male → Mini DisplayPort female
products.fit: 6 in · 4.7 mm OD · not for Thunderbolt displays
products.summary: One passive StarTech.com DP2MDPMF6IN adapter cable for connecting a standard DisplayPort source to a Mini DisplayPort monitor cable or Mini DisplayPort display. It is not a Thunderbolt cable and does not work with Apple Thunderbolt Display A1407 or iMac Target Display Mode. Because the maker's datasheet conflicts on maximum resolution, this page conservatively states 2560 by 1600 at 60 Hz rather than promising 4K.

specs.name: Signal direction
specs.value: Standard DisplayPort source to Mini DisplayPort monitor or cable

specs.name: Resolution evidence note
specs.value: The maker's narrative states 2560 × 1600 at 60 Hz while its feature table claims 3840 × 2400 at 60 Hz; Utiliy does not promise the conflicting higher figure

specs.name: Protocols
specs.value: HBR2, MST, GTC and up to 8-channel audio

specs.name: Not compatible with
specs.value: Thunderbolt displays including Apple A1407, iMac Target Display Mode, HDMI, or USB-C

faqs.q: Which end plugs into the computer?
faqs.a: The full-size DisplayPort male plug connects to the source computer, graphics card, or compatible dock. The Mini DisplayPort female side accepts the display's Mini DisplayPort connection.

faqs.q: Will DP2MDPMF6IN connect an Apple Thunderbolt Display?
faqs.a: No. Mini DisplayPort and Thunderbolt 1 or 2 use a similar connector shape, but this is a DisplayPort adapter and StarTech.com excludes Thunderbolt displays such as Apple A1407.

faqs.q: Will this cable work with iMac Target Display Mode?
faqs.a: No. The manufacturer explicitly excludes iMac Target Display Mode.

faqs.q: Is 4K guaranteed?
faqs.a: No. The manufacturer datasheet contains conflicting resolution statements. Utiliy conservatively publishes 2560 by 1600 at 60 Hz and does not promise the higher 4K figure.

faqs.q: How much connector and cable clearance is required?
faqs.a: Allow for a connector up to 20 millimeters wide, a 4.7 millimeter cable diameter, the six-inch cable length, and a gradual bend beyond the strain relief.
